messages:
bethany: FYI customer CacheCo reporting a wave of 504s and p95 API timeouts starting ~09:10 UTC. Ticket #12345, tenant T-4312. They say it started after a marketing campaign.
jamie: Can you paste the gateway logs + any queue metrics you have? :rotating_light:
bethany: quick grab:
```
time=2026-03-17T09:12:03Z level=warn service=gateway tenant=T-4312 req_id=... status=504 msg="request dropped after queue wait"
```
Prom query (09:09-09:15):
```
continuous_batch_queue_depth{tenant="T-4312"} 1287
continuous_batch_dequeue_p95_ms{tenant="T-4312"} 4200
hosted_gateway_5xx_rate{tenant="T-4312"} 0.056
```
bethany: Also seeing many small, back-to-back requests (payloads ~100-200b) from the same client IP range.
liam: That queue depth is huge. Could be head-of-line blocking from longseq requests? Any long sequences? logs show some requests with seq_len=2048.
jamie: Ok hypothesis: continuous-batcher backlog + a few longseqs are blowing out dequeue latency and pushing requests into gateway deadline. Immediate mitigations:
- throttle tenant concurrency
- enable adaptive-shed/fallback to small-variant model
- temporarily lower max_queue_depth for this tenant
ella: I can flip a throttle now. If we reduce tenant concurrency to 8 and max_queue_depth to 500 we should drain backlog fast. Want me to do it?
bethany: Do it. Tell customer we have a mitigation in flight.
ella: running:
```
# console
PUT /tenants/T-4312/config {"concurrency_limit":8, "max_queue_depth":500}
```
deploy-bot: config-change: tenant_config_update T-4312 by ella at 2026-03-17T09:18:42Z
jamie: After the change, watching metrics:
```
continuous_batch_queue_depth{tenant="T-4312"} -> 420 -> 120 (09:20)
continuous_batch_dequeue_p95_ms{tenant="T-4312"} -> 4200 -> 600
hosted_gateway_5xx_rate{tenant="T-4312"} -> 0.056 -> 0.009
```
bethany: Customer confirms errors dropped and latency improved. :thumbsup:
liam: Great. Next steps:
- run a replay from the ingestion logs to reproduce in staging (use same burst pattern + a few longseqs)
- add an automated alert on continuous_batch_dequeue_p95_ms > 1s for any tenant > 200 queue depth
- consider model-routing fallback when queue_depth > X
jamie: I'll add a temporary guard in routing policy to route new requests for this tenant to the smaller-variant if queue_depth > 400. Also will open an incident ticket and assign postmortem.
bethany: Customer ok with postmortem. Please include reproduction steps and the console command we used. I'll attach to the support ticket.
ella: Filed runbook PR with the throttle + routing steps.
jamie: Incident: INC-2026-0317-01 opened. Owners: jamie, ella. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD.
bethany: Closing the customer loop now. Thanks team. :heart:
summary: CacheCo tenant surge caused continuous-batcher backlog; mitigated by tenant concurrency + max_queue_depth reduction and routing fallback. Metrics and logs attached; postmortem in progress.
